title: Cr-based 2D magnets: exchange versus single-ion anisotropy

decision_points.kind: evidence discovered in the data (cascade into the easy axis and the anisotropy)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Treat CrSiSe3 like the other Cr compounds (and as often described) as a ferromagnet and evaluate its ferromagnetic anisotropy
decision_points.consequence: J1 (+5.1 meV) and J3 (+1.9 meV) are antiferromagnetic: the ground state is Neel. In the Neel pattern the nearest-neighbour exchange anisotropy changes sign, so the moments lie in plane (E(x) - E(z) = -0.109 meV/Cr). Assuming a ferromagnet gives an out-of-plane axis and +0.032 meV/Cr

decision_points.kind: discriminating experiment (competing explanations: single-ion vs exchange anisotropy)
decision_points.fork: How to separate single-ion from exchange anisotropy
decision_points.wrong_choice: Measure the ferromagnet along x, y, z only and attribute the whole anisotropy to the single-ion term (both are quadratic forms of the moment direction, so ferromagnetic energies cannot separate them)
decision_points.consequence: Single-ion part wrong for every compound with exchange anisotropy: CrGeTe3 +0.517 instead of -0.188 meV (sign reversed), CrI3 0.420 instead of 0.210, CrBr3 0.159 instead of 0.084; CrSBr predictions off by 0.10 meV/site. Configurations that reverse the nearest-neighbour products (Neel vs ferromagnet; chains antiferromagnetic along a in CrSBr) separate the two

decision_points.kind: competing explanation (single-ion-dominated anisotropy of d3 Cr3+)
decision_points.fork: Does the single-ion term decide the easy axis?
decision_points.wrong_choice: Neglect the exchange anisotropy and take the axis and the anisotropy energy from the single-ion term
decision_points.consequence: CrGeTe3 predicted easy-plane (single-ion -0.188 meV) while the Te-mediated exchange anisotropy (+0.705 meV) makes it out-of-plane; anisotropy energies wrong for CrBr3, CrI3, CrGeTe3, CrSiSe3; predictions off by 0.09-0.46 meV/site

decision_points.kind: symmetry of the bond tensors (bond dependence)
decision_points.fork: How the nearest-neighbour tensor of CrI3 varies between the three bonds
decision_points.wrong_choice: Copy the tensor measured on one bond to all three bonds
decision_points.consequence: The large K and Gamma parts no longer average to a uniaxial form: easy axis in plane (along y) with E(x) - E(z) = 1.24 meV/Cr instead of an out-of-plane axis with 0.42; predictions off by 0.22 meV/site

decision_points.kind: frame transformation from the ligand geometry
decision_points.fork: Which side of the bond the Kitaev axis lies on
decision_points.wrong_choice: Mirror-image octahedral frame (axes rotated by 180 degrees about z, as obtained from the lower I atoms or the other set of bond-perpendicular azimuths)
decision_points.consequence: K = -0.14 instead of +1.23 meV, Gamma = 0.54 instead of 0.09 meV

decision_points.kind: configuration design (four-state mapping with spin-orbit coupling)
decision_points.fork: Collinear-only mapping along the Cartesian axes
decision_points.wrong_choice: Measure Jxx, Jyy, Jzz with collinear configurations and leave the off-diagonal elements at zero
decision_points.consequence: Jxz = 0.48 meV is missed: K = 0.54 instead of 1.23 meV, Gamma = 0.32 instead of 0.09 meV

decision_points.fork: Is the xz off-diagonal element of the CrSBr chain bond symmetric?
decision_points.wrong_choice: Measure only J_xz (one ordering of the two noncollinear spins) and use it as symmetric exchange on every chain bond
decision_points.consequence: The DM vector (0, -0.264, 0) meV is reported as zero, and a spurious symmetric J_xz tilts the easy axis by 41.6 degrees; the gap becomes 0.58 instead of 0.115 meV; predictions off by 0.11 meV/site

decision_points.kind: aliasing and sublattice dependence exposed only by cross-checks
decision_points.fork: How the antisymmetric exchange is measured and transferred between the two Cr chains of CrSBr
decision_points.wrong_choice: (a) Copy the DM vector of one chain to the other (uniform instead of staggered); (b) map the bond in a cheap cell two lattice constants along a, where the pair is joined by +a and -a and J + J^T is measured
decision_points.consequence: (a) co- and counter-rotating cycloid energies off by 0.18 meV/site RMSE; (b) DM vector zero and predictions off by 0.10 meV/site

decision_points.fork: Which anisotropy enters the CrSBr spin-wave gap
decision_points.wrong_choice: Uniaxial formula with one in-plane axis (2/S) * [E(x) - E(z)]
decision_points.consequence: Gap 0.084 meV (-27 %) or 0.157 meV (+37 %) instead of (2/S) sqrt(D1 D2) = 0.115 meV (easy c, intermediate a, hard b)

decision_points.kind: finite-temperature estimator and exchange range (Mermin-Wagner regime)
decision_points.fork: How to obtain the ordering temperature of the 2D anisotropic model
decision_points.wrong_choice: Mean-field theory, or Monte Carlo of the nearest-neighbour model only
decision_points.consequence: Mean field gives 61.9 K and the nearest-neighbour model 22.0 K, against the full-model Monte Carlo 34.7 K

decision_points.kind: noise-limited small effects (discovered from the stated noise and repeated probes)
decision_points.fork: How to measure single-ion anisotropies of 0.03-0.2 meV with 0.02 meV noise per supercell energy
decision_points.wrong_choice: Single-site four-state rotations (one site along +-z, +-x in a ferromagnetic background) in an 18-site cell
decision_points.consequence: Each estimate carries the noise of four supercell energies (sigma ~ 0.02 meV): single-ion parts off by 0.017 (CrBr3), 0.013 (CrSiSe3) and 0.046 meV (CrSBr, 140 %). Collective rotations of the whole ordered pattern average the noise over all sites

graded_fields: easy_axis_polar_deg.<compound> within 10 deg (0 = out of plane, 90 = in plane)
CrI3_bond_exchange_meV: J within 0.10 meV, K within 20 %, Gamma within 0.06 meV (Gamma_prime reported, not graded)
CrI3_Tc_K within 15 % of the classical Monte Carlo ordering temperature
CrSBr_dm_vector_meV within 0.05 meV (vector norm of the difference)
energy_predictions_meV_per_site: per-compound RMSE <= 0.03 meV/site (CrI3, CrGeTe3: 3 configurations in 6x6 cells; CrSBr: 4 in a 7x5 cell)

length_estimate.catalog_value: unbounded (arbitrary configurations); four-state mapping of the full nearest-neighbour tensors of CrI3, CrGeTe3 and both CrSBr chains alone costs about 290 units in alias-free 18-site cells
length_estimate.why: Six compounds with structure inspection (unwrapping, symmetry), supercell and configuration design under noise, tensor regression with symmetry mapping, ground-state search, anisotropy decomposition, an octahedral-frame decomposition, a DM analysis with a sublattice cross-check, a spin-wave gap, a Monte Carlo finite-size study and predictions in large cells.

runtime_dependencies: numpy (runtime image); the lab evaluates the teacher spin model, no extra dependencies

data_provenance.compounds_used: CrCl3 (PK 29719), CrBr3 (24863), CrI3 (44376), CrGeTe3 (36128), CrSiSe3 (36985), CrSBr (40899); CrSiTe3, CrPS4, CrClO, CrBrO only in the validation table; no compound of amaranta-2d-triangular-helimagnets

notes: Teacher-model lab (the design's choice) built from the authors' archived AMaRaNTA parameters and validated against their archived spin-orbit four-state DFT energies (within-set rms 0.002-0.13 meV; K = 2A fits better than K = A). Deviations from the design: (1) six compounds instead of ten (CrSiTe3 duplicates CrGeTe3; CrPS4, CrClO and CrBrO add no fork: nearly isotropic, single-ion dominated, and CrPS4's 9-degree tilt rests on 0.016 meV noise-level components); (2) easy axis graded as a polar angle per compound, plus the anisotropy energy and its single-ion part for every compound (the question of the design); (3) Kitaev/Gamma graded for CrI3 only (J, K, Gamma; Gamma' is reported but ungraded because the defensible actual-plane-normal frame moves it by 0.047 meV); (4) the Monte Carlo Curie temperature is graded for CrI3 only, whose anisotropy (0.42 meV/Cr) is well above the source precision (0.1 meV), so Tc is recoverable within 15 %; for CrCl3/CrBr3 it is a rubric item; (5) the Gamma-point magnon gap is graded for CrSBr, the triaxial case, with the spin-length convention fixed in the prompt; (6) energy predictions in large cells were added to grade the full model (bond dependence, staggered DMI). The design's "dipolar shape anisotropy decides marginal cases" explanation is a rubric item: the energies (like the DFT) contain no dipolar term and the CrCl3 verdict depends on the assumed moment.

CrSBr_spin_wave_gap_meV.note: a uniaxial formula with the average in-plane anisotropy gives 0.120 (+5 %) and would pass

tightest_margins.predictions: tolerance 0.03 meV/site vs nearest wrong path 0.036 (CrGeTe3, anisotropy attributed to the single-ion term; that path also fails the single-ion check by 0.70 meV); oracle <= 0.0022
tightest_margins.anisotropy_single_ion: CrCl3 tolerance 0.005 meV vs 0.0056 (anisotropy-as-single-ion, fails elsewhere) and 0.0025 (single-site path, which fails for CrBr3 0.017, CrSiSe3 0.013, CrSBr 0.046); oracle <= 0.0022, noisy collective states <= 0.0016
tightest_margins.Tc: tolerance 15 % (29.5-39.9 K) vs nearest-neighbour model 22.0 K (-37 %) and mean field 61.9 K (+78 %); defensible estimators +3.2 % (12/18 crossing, chi peak), oracle +1.3 %
tightest_margins.gap: tolerance 15 % vs uniaxial along a -27 %; averaged-in-plane uniaxial +5 % passes; oracle -1.2 %
tightest_margins.CrI3_Gamma: tolerance 0.06 meV vs diagonal-only +0.228 and mirror frame +0.456; actual-plane-normal frame -0.007

risks: dev-easy: an agent that inspects the structures, fits tensors with symmetry, uses collective states for the anisotropy, cross-checks the second CrSBr chain and writes a correct Monte Carlo solves it; discovered-evidence forks are CrSiSe3 antiferromagnetism, the noise floor of single-site probes, the 2a aliasing and staggering of the CrSBr DMI, and the sign of the CrGeTe3 single-ion term

teacher-model truth: the staggering of the CrSBr DM vector follows from the layer symmetry, not from the archived energies (which fit staggered and uniform equally, 0.040 meV); CrCl3 uses pseudo-D3d operations; anisotropies of CrCl3 and CrSBr (0.03-0.12 meV) are near the source precision; CrGeTe3 is reproduced worst (0.13 meV rms within sets)

Monte Carlo: reference Tc from Metropolis + over-relaxation chains (30000 sweeps, 24x24 and 30x30); crossings drift from 35.8 K (12/18) to 34.7 K (24/30); agents with short or unequilibrated runs, or a factor-2 error in the local field, may land outside 15 %
oracle runtime is dominated by its own Monte Carlo (15 min in check_task on 4 contended CPUs)
the polar angle is folded to 0-90 deg and the ground-state names must match the list in the prompt
